_comment: Golden cases for ingredient matching, taken from real lines in the corpus.
Every entry here is a bug that was found by reading output, and would
otherwise be reintroduced by the next ranking change. Matching is heuristic
plus a curated table, and both are the kind of thing where fixing one food
silently breaks another — a first-segment rule once fixed milk and beef and
cost thirteen points of coverage on bread crumbs. This file is how that gets
expect  — a substring the matched USDA description must contain (case-insensitive)
reject  — a substring it must NOT contain; this is the wrong answer we saw
found   — where the line came from, so a failure can be checked against the page
Add a case whenever a miss is noticed. Never delete one to make a suite pass.

cases.found: Natasha's Kitchen — 'chopped' stems to 'chop' under the Porter tokenizer
Serious Eats — the unit word 'cloves' is itself a food
several — a single short term gives bm25 nothing to rank on
several — 'ground' was wrongly treated as preparation, leaving only 'beef'
Serious Eats — a first-segment rule sent this to 'Coffee cake, crumb type'
several — USDA files the cup portion under the older spelling
several — 'Toaster pastries, brown-sugar-cinnamon' is a near miss
Natasha's Kitchen — matched 'Peppers, bell, red, raw'
the density case: leaves 1.0 g/tsp vs ground 1.8 g/tsp

rejections.found: Serious Eats — must not be given a quantity

coverageFloor.note: Coverage on the meatloaf corpus must not regress below this. It was 46% before the stemming and dataset-preference fixes, 69% after, and 75% once the alias table landed. Raise this number when it is genuinely beaten; never lower it to make a change pass.
